The Sr Product Owner plays a critical role in ensuring that a product or feature is developed with a focus on delivering value to the customer and the business. They act as a voice for the customer and are responsible for making key product-related decisions throughout the development process, including identifying opportunities to incorporate emerging technologies, such as AI-enabled capabilities, where they can improve user experience, workflow efficiency, and business outcomes.

Product Vision & Stakeholder Alignment
Translation: Work with stakeholders to translate future vision and requirements into clearly broken-down epics and stories; ensure all team members understand and align with product goals, including consideration of emerging technologies where appropriate.
Stakeholder Communication: Act as the primary point of contact between the development team and stakeholders; communicate progress, changes, and updates regularly.
Team Enabler: Work with one or more Agile Development Teams and act as a central reference and information source, guiding system/product functionality decisions.
Entrepreneurial Spirit: Demonstrate a track record of delivering results in fast-moving, demanding environments.
Backlog Ownership & Prioritization
Prioritization: Create and maintain the product backlog; prioritize features, user stories, and tasks based on business value, customer needs, market trends, and strategic opportunities.
Backlog Management: Continuously groom and refine the backlog based on feedback, changing priorities, and new insights.
Feedback Integration: Gather and incorporate feedback from stakeholders and end-users into the backlog; adjust as necessary.

User Story Development: Break down high-level requirements into detailed, implementable user stories that meet strong Agile standards and support effective workflows, automation, and decision support where applicable.
Acceptance Criteria: Define clear acceptance criteria so the team understands what constitutes “done” for each feature.
UI/UX Alignment: Partner with UX to ensure backlog items have wireframes and UI designs ready for sprint planning; provide design feedback, participate in design sprints, and support user acceptance testing.
Planning, Delivery & Risk
Sprint Planning: Participate in sprint planning to select stories and tasks; ensure the team has a clear understanding of work scope.
Release Planning: Collaborate with the team and stakeholders to plan and prioritize releases aligned with market needs and business goals.
Quality Assurance: Ensure the product meets quality standards by accepting or rejecting work during sprint reviews.
Risk Management: Identify and mitigate delivery risks; partner with the release manager on timelines, tough conversations, mitigation strategies, and transparent escalation to leadership.
Business Outcomes & Data
Business Case Support: Assist in developing and presenting business cases for new features and initiatives; ensure alignment with strategic goals and stakeholder expectations.
Data-Driven: Define KPIs and measures for features and capabilities to track impact and inform decisions.

We are hiring a Product Manager to drive our Zero Trust Authentication group. In this role, you will lead the core execution, performance, and deployment strategy for Okta’s foundational endpoint products. You will own the operational excellence of Okta Verify , FastPass , and Device Assurance , ensuring that our core passwordless authentication flows and device posture engines remain performant, secure, and incredibly easy for global enterprises to deploy at scale.

This is a critical, high-impact role designed for a highly autonomous product manager. You will take on the tactical execution and smaller strategic investments for our endpoint authenticators, acting as the team's operational anchor so that our senior product leaders can continuously expand our strategic frontiers.

What you will own

You will bridge user experience and deep systems engineering to ensure our core authentication products scale reliably for millions of global users.

· Core Device Assurance Execution: Own the roadmap for our baseline security posture checks (such as OS version validation, disk encryption, and firewall status). You will manage the execution of our posture policy engine and our first-party EDR/MDM signal integrations.

· Okta Verify Core Features: You will lead the feature roadmap and runtime capabilities for Okta Verify across iOS, Android, macOS, Windows, and Linux. You will focus on transforming raw device-side signals into secure user experiences, managing the lifecycle of on-device authenticators, and shipping tactical feature enhancements.

· Frictionless FastPass Adoption: You will drive the enrollment, registration, and adoption feature loops for FastPass, our premier passwordless, phishing-resistant authenticator. You will build zero-touch MDM provisioning paths, streamlined setup flows, and deployment controls that make passwordless authentication frictionless to activate.

A day in the life

Your day is a constant balancing act between core platform execution and immediate customer support. You might start your morning on a call with a strategic customer, taking tactical feedback on a Device Assurance integration and helping them design a phased rollout plan to migrate their users to FastPass. By midday, you are partnering with your engineering leads and software architects, debating the technical trade-offs of a client-side storage upgrade or reviewing app startup latency metrics.

By midday, you shift your focus to execution. You thrive on taking highly ambiguous problem spaces and bringing absolute clarity to the engineering teams. You partner deeply with your engineering leads and architects, debating technical trade-offs and ensuring that project requirements are clearly defined, scoped, and directly tied to delivering concrete solutions for our customers.

In the afternoon, you collaborate with your product peers to ensure that foundational device signals map cleanly to downstream capabilities like Identity Threat Protection or core policy evaluations. You write highly detailed, plain-prose specifications with clear problem statements to guide developer execution.

You close the day working with our Go-To-Market and support teams, ensuring they have the technical documentation and tooling needed to diagnose customer issues, resolve endpoint friction, and drive up FastPass activation rates.

Scale is accelerating the development of AI across the world's most important organizations, including the U.S. Department of War (DoW), its constituent services, and the broader U.S. National Security industry. The Product Manager, Public Sector will lead Scale's product efforts across two connected focus areas — military planning and real-time AI and Alerting (LUX) — shaping real production outcomes and translating messy operational reality into high-signal input for the core platform.

This is not a roadmap PM, a CSM, or a solutions engineer.

This PM owns product outcomes for a cross-cutting portfolio of AI and data capabilities: earning deep trust with senior military, civilian, and mission stakeholders, driving deployments to production inside classified and operationally constrained environments, identifying where the product is the bottleneck vs. execution, and feeding durable, specific signal back to Scale's platform team.

The best candidates have shipped AI or real-time data products into defense or other large, security-constrained organizations and can tell the difference between a customer's stated request, their actual problem, and what the platform should do.

· Own product outcomes across Scale's military planning portfolio and/or its highest-impact national security accounts for LUX, spanning multiple DoW and National Security stakeholders and use cases. You are the accountable PM for product delivery and customer value.

· Translate operational reality into high-signal product input for engineering and platform teams — specific, evidence-backed product perspective with tradeoffs articulated, not requirements docs. This includes military planning workflows (e.g., the Joint Planning Process) and modeling/simulation requirements (e.g., AFSIM), as well as real customer workflows, latency/throughput constraints, and mission priorities for LUX.

· Build trusted advisory relationships with senior military leaders (flag/general officer and senior civilian equivalents), National Security customer stakeholders, and senior technical leads. Become the reliable escalation point on the Scale side before issues surface externally.

· Drive deployments from contract to production inside classified and operationally constrained environments — whether that means military planning workflows or LUX's low-latency, high-throughput, mission-critical data systems. You know what "production-ready" means inside DoW, and you close the gap.

· Distinguish where the product is the constraint from where execution, integration, policy, or change management is the constraint. Drive each type of blocker to resolution through the right channel.

· Shape a cross-cutting set of solutions spanning multiple stakeholders, echelons, and use cases, rather than owning a single point deployment.

· Partner closely with Forward Deployed Engineering (FDE) teams and Platform Capability teams so the account runs as a coordinated team, not a set of parallel workstreams.

· Identify and develop expansion opportunities grounded in demonstrated customer value.

· Represent customer reality to the platform and leadership with enough credibility that it changes decisions.

· Balance competing requirements across CCMDs and service components that must collaborate despite differing needs — distinct from building for a single customer.

· Travel as required to customer sites, including classified facilities.

· Enterprise deployment ownership : has driven AI/ML or complex/real-time software products from contract to production at scale — including near-zero-to-one, with no real users yet — with real integration, real security constraints, and real change management.

· Domain fluency : working knowledge of the military planning process and modeling/simulation tools (e.g., Joint Planning Process, AFSIM), and/or the tradeoffs inherent to real-time, event-driven, high-throughput data architectures and their implications for AI agents — and how each shapes product decisions.

· Product judgment in the field : translates customer reality into product direction, not just feature requests; can say no credibly and explain why.

· Customer trust-building : earns and maintains trust with demanding senior military, civilian, and mission stakeholders over multi-quarter engagements; manages conflict without eroding the relationship.

· Technical translation : bridges the gap between customer engineering/planning teams and Scale platform engineers; adds interpretation rather than simply relaying messages.

· Operating in ambiguity and constrained environments : creates structure where there is none; makes decisions with incomplete information inside classified settings; does not wait for fully defined requirements.

· Clear, precise communication : adjusts for audience (senior leader vs. engineer vs. PM); writes and speaks at the right level of detail; does not over- or under-explain.

· Active TOP SECRET security clearance (TS/SCI eligibility preferred).

· 6+ years in product management, technical program management, or a customer-facing product ownership role, including experience operating at an L6 (senior/staff) level of scope and autonomy.

· Direct experience working with the U.S. Department of War (DoW) or the broader U.S. national security community.

· Working knowledge of at least one of the following, with an ability to speak credibly to the other:

· The military planning process (e.g., the Joint Planning Process) and modeling/simulation systems (e.g., AFSIM).

· Real-time streaming data systems — event-driven architectures, low-latency pipelines, and high-throughput data processing — and how they behave in production.

· Demonstrated record of shipping AI or data products into large, constrained, classified, or highly regulated organizations — not pilots or proofs-of-concept. You can name the customer, the scale, the integration, and what production actually looked like.

· Extreme ownership and follow-through: closes loops without reminders, drives outcomes across teams without formal authority, holds self and others to commitments.

· Comfortable operating with senior military/civilian/mission stakeholders and senior engineers simultaneously; credible presence in high-stakes rooms on both sides.

· Strong judgment under pressure: makes good calls quickly with incomplete information, knows when to escalate vs. resolve, does not generate thrash.

· Technical fluency sufficient to hold a real conversation with a platform engineer about architectural tradeoffs — not deep coding, but genuine comprehension of how systems work in production.

· Ability to shape a cross-cutting set of solutions across multiple stakeholders and use cases, rather than customer-specific solutions.

· Ability to travel, including to classified facilities.

· Direct experience with AI/ML platform products — agentic capabilities, human-agent interaction, large-scale data, some T&E; or data labeling, RLHF, fine-tuning workflows, and model evaluation pipelines.

· Hands-on familiarity with streaming technologies (e.g., Kafka, Flink, Kinesis) or the operational systems that consume them.

Who we are

About Stripe

Stripe is a financial infrastructure platform for businesses. Millions of companies—from the world’s largest enterprises to the most ambitious startups—use Stripe to accept payments, grow their revenue, and accelerate new business opportunities. Our mission is to increase the GDP of the internet, and we have a staggering amount of work ahead. That means you have an unprecedented opportunity to put the global economy within everyone’s reach while doing the most important work of your career.

About the Product - Connect Platform

Connect is Stripe’s platform for businesses that serve other businesses. It gives platforms the infrastructure to represent the people and companies in their ecosystem, onboard and verify them, manage their accounts, accept payments, and pay them out - without building payments, compliance, or financial-services systems themselves.

This is how businesses like Shopify can help entrepreneurs run and grow their businesses. It is also the kind of infrastructure that marketplaces such as DoorDash need to coordinate money movement across large networks of restaurants, merchants, and dashers.

Connect has impact across industries. Shopify uses Stripe to embed financial services for merchants; Lugg streamlines worker onboarding and offers instant payouts; DoorLoop reduces manual customer onboarding tasks by nearly 50% with Stripe; and Sharetribe helps entrepreneurs launch and run marketplaces on Stripe.

AI is accelerating the emergence of entirely new business models: global networks of creators and experts, AI-native marketplaces, and agent-driven products that change how people discover, buy, sell, and deliver services. These businesses are more dynamic than traditional platforms: participants may operate across borders, take on different roles, and need new ways to establish trust, access financial capabilities, and get paid.

The Connect Abstractions team owns the platform primitives that make these models possible. We are building the foundational abstractions for representing participants, onboarding them safely, configuring their capabilities, and managing their lifecycle on Stripe. Our work will determine how quickly the next generation of platforms can launch, how flexibly they can evolve, and how much of Stripe they can bring to the businesses and people they serve.

Why this role

This is a chance to define a foundational product area at Stripe. You will turn a fast-changing set of user and product needs into durable platform primitives that work across products, industries, and geographies.

The role combines high-leverage strategy with hands-on product execution. You will work through ambiguous, consequential questions like: what should a platform be able to model? What should be simple by default but flexible when needed? How can Stripe make complex financial infrastructure feel effortless for a platform and its users?

The outcome of your work will compound. The abstractions you help create will be reused across Connect and Stripe, shaping what new products platforms can build and how quickly they can bring them to market.

We are looking for an entrepreneurial Product Manager to build the platform experiences behind Connect's next generation of users. You will own critical product primitives that platforms, including the fastest-growing AI companies, use to onboard, configure, and manage their users on Stripe. You will turn a clear strategic direction into products that solve hard user problems today while creating a coherent, extensible foundation for business models that are still being invented.

This role is for someone who enjoys the depth of platform work but is uncompromising about product craft and solving real user needs - both the ones users have today and will have in the future. The work is not building infra for its own sake; you will build capabilities that help our users launch a new marketplace, enable a global network to pay its contributors, or give a business entirely new ways for their end users to earn.

· Bring the next generation of Connect accounts to life. Own key product areas within the account platform, translating strategy into a focused roadmap, crisp product decisions, and high-quality launches.

· Build from use cases. Start with the real problems platforms face, such as onboarding a new seller, supporting a complex business model, or evolving a user's financial capabilities, and then work towards the primitives needed to solve them well.

· Make sophisticated infrastructure feel simple. Partner with engineering and design to create API and product experiences that are powerful and intuitive.

· See around corners. Develop a strong point of view on how AI will change platform economics, participant models, and financial workflows. Make focused foundational investments that unlock the next wave of demand.

· Turn user signals into durable product investments. Work closely with users, Sales, Partnerships, and other Stripe teams to distinguish bespoke requests from patterns that should become scalable platform capabilities, connecting business needs, user needs, and platform evolution.

· Drive high-velocity, high-craft execution and own outcomes. Lead cross-functional work from discovery through launch, and hold yourself accountable for developer experience, platform adoption, user value, and business impact, not simply features shipped.

We’re looking for someone who meets the minimum requirements to be considered for the role. If you meet these requirements, you are encouraged to apply. The preferred qualifications are a bonus, not a requirement.

· You are a product builder who can move easily between a user’s hardest problem, the business opportunity behind it, and the product decisions needed to solve it.

· You have worked on technically complex products - such as APIs, developer tools, shared platform capabilities, or core product experiences - but you do not build tech/platform for its own sake. You see strong platform design as a way to help users move faster, create better products, and unlock new business models.

· You are opinionated, thoughtful, and execution-oriented. You can focus a team on the few decisions that matter most, create momentum in ambiguous situations, and ship products that raise the bar for both quality and impact.

· Demonstrated ability to own a product area end to end: setting strategy, driving execution, and measuring outcomes

· Strong analytical instincts and comfort defining the measurement framework before you ship

· Clear written communication and the ability to build alignment across functions and levels

· Experience in payments, fintech, or financial infrastructure

· Experience productizing bespoke or custom solutions into broadly available platform capabilities

· A track record of making well-judged foundational investments ahead of user demand

Join the team as Twilio’s next Staff, Data Product Manager, GTM Data Science & Analytics.

We are seeking a Staff, Data Product Manager to lead the strategy, development roadmap, and lifecycle of our data products and platforms. In this role, you will work at the intersection of data, technology, and business to unlock the value of data across the organization.

You’ll define the roadmap for data solutions, collaborate with cross-functional teams, and ensure data products are scalable, reliable, and user-friendly. Together we’ll turn fragmented, raw data into structured, usable assets that drive decision-making, automation, and personalization across teams.

You’ll ensure the right data is accessible, trustworthy, and actionable to power everything from executive insights to predictive models. You’ll bridge the gap between technical teams who build data infrastructure and business teams who rely on it, aligning data strategy with business goals.

In short, you will turn data into our most valuable asset to drive business growth.

· Define and own the vision, strategy, and roadmap for data products (e.g., dashboards, data platforms, model features and enhancements, etc) that support data-driven insights, decisioning, and actions.

· Act as the bridge between data engineers, data scientists, analysts, and business stakeholders to translate business needs into data solutions.

· Develop product requirements and user stories focused on data access, usability, performance, and quality.

· Prioritize data initiatives based on business impact, technical feasibility, and data availability.

· Ensure proper data governance, privacy, and compliance practices are followed.

· Ensure teams have self-service access to GTM data via platforms, tools, and interfaces.

· Monitor and improve data quality, reliability, and user adoption of data tools and features, providing regular reporting on effectiveness and areas for improvement..

· Define and track success metrics for data products, ensuring they meet business and technical goals.

· Foster a culture of data-driven decision making by making data products intuitive and accessible.

· Partner with finance, product, and sales teams to ensure that data products serve the needs of our internal customers.

· Stay informed about industry trends, tools, and best practices in data product management and data enablement.

· Develop training materials to empower teams across the organization to use data effectively for decision-making, campaign execution, and customer engagement.

What to Expect from the Hiring Process We believe hiring should feel like a conversation, not a test. Here’s what you can expect if you apply: Step 1 — Conversation with People & Culture (30 minutes) If your experience looks like a fit, you’ll meet with our Head of People & Culture for a video chat.

It’s a two-way conversation, we’ll learn about your background, skills, and what energizes you, and you’ll have space to ask about Revaly , our mission, and what it’s like to work here. It’s also a chance to make sure the vibes are right on both sides.

Step 2 — Conversation with the Hiring Manager (60 minutes) Next, you’ll meet with the hiring manager for a deeper dive into your role-specific experience. We’ll talk through real scenarios, how you approach challenges, and what success looks like in this role. You’ll also get a clearer picture of the team’s goals and priorities.

Step 3 — Meet a Future Teammate (60 minutes) In this stage, you’ll meet with someone from the team you’ll work closely with. This is your chance to get an on-the-ground perspective, how the team collaborates, what day-to-day looks like, and the kind of people you’ll be building alongside.

Step 4 — 90 Day Ramp Up Presentation (30 minutes) In this final stage, we ask candidates to prepare and present a 90 day ramp up plan to the hiring manager. This is an opportunity for candidates to outline how they would approach their first 3 months in the role, what they’d aim to learn, prioritize, and accomplish.

This is a chance to show your understanding of the role, the company, and the environment we’re operating in, while giving the hiring manager a glimpse into how you think, structure your approach to learning and communicate your ideas.

We hire for both skill and fit, looking for people who are not just aligned with our values, but who will add to our culture with their ideas, energy, and perspective.

If you’ve applied for a role in Technology or Product Development, you can also expect a skill-based assessment between step 3 and 4, to help us assess some key role-based requirements.

Accommodation is available upon request for applicants with disabilities.

We're an extremely collaborative group, and we host frequent research discussions to ensure that we are pursuing the highest-impact work at any given time. Working as a Product Manager at MG AI
While engineers focus on building and shipping models, Product Managers at MG AI own the why and the what. We translate complex, often ambiguous business challenges from Match Group's brands into clear ML product strategy, and we drive execution across a globally distributed team. The PMs who thrive here are strategic troubleshooters with a bias for action: they spot what is blocking progress and drive it to resolution instead of waiting.
This is a communication-first role, but that does not mean coordination alone. Your core job is to figure out which problem is worth solving, articulate it in clear and precise language, and drive alignment among a diverse set of stakeholders across cultures and time zones. You own the product thinking end to end: framing the problem, shaping the plan, and defining what we build.
You will work on projects that leverage a wide range of technologies, from on-device ML modules to server-side AI models and LLMs. You do not need to be an ML expert on day one, but you must learn fast and become technically fluent enough to make sound product calls, because the technology and the problems keep changing.

Frame the Problem: Figure out which problems are worth solving and why, and articulate them in clear, precise language that a diverse team can rally around.
Shape the Roadmap: Decide what matters most, sequence the work, make the tradeoffs, and write PRDs, keeping partners aligned as priorities shift.
Navigate Complex Stakeholder Maps: Act as the connective tissue between Match Group's brands, and the many functions within them, and MG AI engineering. Read the unspoken dynamics, build alignment across brands, functions, cultures, and time zones, and keep everyone moving in the same direction.
Hands-on Execution: Stay deeply involved in the details. Use experiments, behavioral data, and research to guide your calls when signals are imperfect, unblock engineering, and make the small decisions that keep a project moving.

Exceptional Communication & Stakeholder Management (most important): You excel at managing stakeholders in complex, high-ambiguity situations. You read between the lines, sense interpersonal and organizational dynamics, and build alignment across teams with competing priorities. This is the single most important quality for this role.
4-6 years of product management experience in the Tech domain, ideally on complex systems or data or ML-driven products.

Analytical Rigor: Comfort with data. You can define metrics, design and read experiments, and let evidence guide your decisions.
Global Operational Readiness: Ability to accommodate flexible working hours for regular early morning syncs with US teams (EST/PST).

A Point of View on AI Tooling: A clear sense of how AI tools can raise the quality and speed of product work, and a habit of using them (e.g., Claude, ChatGPT, Cursor).

This role sits within APEX (AI Foundations), the team building the platform-level infrastructure behind ServiceNow's enterprise AI strategy. You'll work alongside engineering, data, and applied research partners to make evaluation a durable, compounding advantage.

Agentic AI is only as trustworthy as the evaluation discipline behind it. ServiceNow is building the evaluation methodology, tooling, and closed-loop production system that will define how good is good enough for AI specialists and multi-agent frameworks across the enterprise — and we're looking for the product leader to help own that discipline.

This is a rare chance to build a category-defining evaluation platform from the ground up, at a company where the outcome shapes how every business unit ships AI, not just one team's roadmap.
Why this role matters
Evaluation is the foundational differentiator for enterprise agentic AI. As frontier models commoditize, defensible advantage shifts to the orchestration and quality layer — how reliably an AI specialist performs in a customer's production environment. This role sits at exactly that inflection point:
You set direction in undefined space — there is no existing playbook to inherit, and the discipline you build becomes the standard others build on.
Your impact is horizontal and enterprise-wide by design, driven through influence, tooling, and a Center of Excellence rather than headcount.
You'll be the definitive point of reference for AI specialist quality across the portfolio — deep technical and methodological ownership without the dilution of people management.
Success is visible and concrete: your framework adopted across business units, a closed-loop system demonstrably improving specialists release-over-release, and tooling used self-serve by teams you never directly staffed.
The impact you'll make
Evaluation strategy and framework: Define the end-to-end evaluation methodology across ServiceNow's AI specialist portfolio — golden datasets, LLM-as-judge calibration, failure taxonomy, and a multi-layer metric model spanning agent behavior, user experience, and business impact.

We're looking for a Staff Product Manager to own the vision and roadmap for Render's datastores portfolio, with our Postgres offering at the center. You will define what a modern managed database experience looks like, including how database products will adapt to new state patterns from agents and how agents as users of state-keeping products should be accommodated.
You'll drive the technical and strategic direction for Render Postgres and our broader data layer, working directly with your team and infrastructure engineering to shape architectural decisions. You'll engage with Render's customers and our product development teams to develop a deep understanding of their data needs and build conviction about where the datastores portfolio needs to go next.

Own the vision, strategy, and roadmap for Render's datastores, anchored on Postgres. Your scope spans provisioning and lifecycle management, high availability and disaster recovery, backups and point-in-time recovery, scaling and performance, connection management, and the extension ecosystem.
Drive prioritization across Render's data investments, balancing the leverage of foundational reliability work — replication, failover, storage performance — against near-term product and business needs, and being able to negotiate those tradeoffs.
Partner deeply with Engineering & other Product teams to shape the technical direction of Render's data layer, ensuring architectural decisions optimize for durability, performance, and operational simplicity. Databases are where customer trust is won or lost, so an instinct for reliability and data safety is essential.
Develop a strong, opinionated point of view on how managed Postgres needs to evolve to serve AI-native builders — from vector workloads and retrieval pipelines to databases that are spun up, branched, and torn down programmatically by agents at scale.
Set the standard for how developers experience data on Render, providing clear guidance, sensible defaults, and abstractions that make it easy for teams to run production databases with confidence — without needing a DBA on staff.

7+ years in Product Management, with the majority spent on databases, data infrastructure, developer tools, or platform products.
Familiarity with Postgres — its architecture, operational model, ecosystem, and the tradeoffs teams face running it in production. Bonus if you have strong perspective on how agentic workloads and AI-native applications are reshaping database usage patterns.
Deep developer empathy, for both internal engineering teams and our customers, and the technical depth to make sound architectural tradeoffs in collaboration with engineering.
A track record of taking ambiguous, high-stakes reliability and infrastructure problems and turning them into clear strategy and shipped outcomes.
Strong communication and storytelling skills.

About Faire

Faire is a technology wholesale platform built on the belief that the future is local. Independent retailers around the globe collectively represent a multi-hundred-billion-dollar wholesale market that has historically been fragmented and offline.

At Faire, we're using the power of tech, data, and machine learning to connect this thriving community of entrepreneurs across the globe. Picture your favorite boutique in town — we help them discover the best products from around the world to sell in their stores.

With the right tools and insights, we believe that we can level the playing field so businesses can grow and local communities can thrive.

We’re looking for smart, resourceful and passionate people to join us as we power the shop local movement. If you believe in community, come join ours.

Faire's financial products are among the most powerful and differentiated value props we offer — and among the most consequential for both sides of our marketplace. We extend net-60 and net-90 payment terms to retailers on behalf of brands, offer the Faire Pay credit card with 3% back on purchases, and are actively building brand financing.

These products do something our partners simply cannot do on their own: absorb risk, deploy capital efficiently, and unlock purchasing behavior that drives growth across the platform.

We're looking for a Principal Product Manager to own the entire Faire Pay portfolio — someone who can run disciplined day-to-day execution on Faire Pay while simultaneously developing the longer-term strategic roadmap for how financial products evolve as a core business line. This means thinking clearly about unit economics and cost of capital, building conviction around where Faire has durable competitive advantages, and shipping products that move real business metrics.

· Own strategy and roadmap for Faire's financial products. Set the multi-year direction for how Faire Pay, net terms, brand financing, and future financial products evolve, and build the prioritized, financially grounded roadmap to get there.

· Drive Faire Pay adoption and marketplace impact. Expand the invited retailer cohort, improve activation and retention across the funnel, and demonstrate that financial products are a meaningful growth lever for the core marketplace, not just a standalone offering.

· Own the unit economics. Think in contribution margin, cost of capital, and payback periods. Optimize interchange, manage loss rates, and identify where structural advantages exist versus where we need to earn our way in.

· Partner deeply across Finance, Risk, Legal, Data Science, and Engineering. Earn trust across functions, lead without authority, and keep complex, multi-stakeholder work moving without losing momentum.

· Build the infrastructure for scale. Partner to develop the data infrastructure, risk frameworks, and operational foundations needed to grow financial products responsibly, from underwriting logic to regulatory compliance.

· Communicate clearly at every altitude. Translate complex, technical topics (cost of capital, credit risk, underwriting tradeoffs) for a wide range of audiences, from engineering partners to senior leadership.

· 10+ years of product management experience, with demonstrated ability to own complex, cross-functional products end to end.

· Genuine fintech depth. You've built and shipped financial products — credit, lending, payments, BNPL, or similar — and you understand the mechanics: underwriting logic, cost of capital, credit risk, contribution margin, and regulatory constraints. You don't need to be a finance expert, but you need to be able to lead the room.

· Business equation fluency. You think comfortably in unit economics. You can model whether a new product makes sense given Faire's cost of capital, estimate cohort-level payback periods, and identify structural advantages worth betting on.

· Strategic clarity with hands-on execution. You can zoom out and develop a defensible multi-year point of view, then zoom back in to write crisp PRDs, drive sprint-level execution, and unblock your team.

· Customer and business model empathy. You deeply understand how retailers and brands run their businesses — their cash flow cycles, how they think about credit and payment terms, and what makes them trust a financial product. You design around customer needs, not just what's technically feasible.

· Cross-functional influence across Finance, Risk, Legal, Data Science, and Engineering, and a track record of aligning diverse stakeholders while maintaining momentum.

· Structured problem solving. You break ambiguous problems into clear hypotheses, don't mistake activity for progress, and diagnose root causes rather than escalate.

· High learning velocity. Financial products sit at the intersection of marketplace dynamics, risk, and regulatory complexity.

· Proven ability to influence at the executive level and to communicate complex topics with clarity and conviction across audiences.

· B2B marketplace experience is a strong plus — particularly familiarity with two-sided dynamics, competing customer objectives, and the structural differences between B2B and consumer credit.

San Francisco, CA/New York City, NY: The pay range for this role is $260,000 - $357,500 per year.

This role will also be eligible for equity and benefits. Actual base pay will be determined based on permissible factors, including transferable skills, work experience, market demand, and primary work location. The base pay range provided is subject to change and may be modified in the future.

This role owns the Business Central ERP platform for Mews — the financial engine connecting every transaction, journal entry, and regulatory obligation across the business.

The person in this seat is one of two product owners across the entire finance ERP estate, working directly with finance stakeholders across accounts payable, accounts receivable, controlling, general ledger, tax, and reporting to turn operational pain points into engineering delivery.

Mews is building the financial infrastructure that audit-ready, high-growth SaaS companies need at scale — and this role shapes what that looks like.

You will own the Business Central backlog across six finance pillars, setting the roadmap, prioritising with stakeholders, and working directly with internal engineers to deliver. You will be the bridge between finance teams who present precise, point-in-time problems and the engineering team that needs clear, actionable specifications.

You will also evaluate Microsoft's quarterly and biannual release cycles, translate incoming regulatory requirements into delivery items, and manage integrations with treasury management tooling and open banking infrastructure. · Translate regulatory requirements, including mandatory e-invoicing and audit-readiness obligations, into roadmap items with clear delivery plans

· Define KPIs for ERP initiatives and drive continuous improvement across finance and operational workflows

· Hands-on ERP experience, ideally in Microsoft Dynamics 365 Business Central; Dynamics 365 F&O, NetSuite, Workday, or Odoo are also considered

· Direct collaboration with internal software engineers on ERP delivery — not exclusively third-party implementation partners

· Product ownership or delivery experience: backlog management, epic decomposition, and stakeholder prioritisation across parallel demands

· Breadth across finance processes — you understand more than one pillar and can hold the bigger picture alongside the detail

· You have gone beyond personal AI productivity: you have redesigned how you or a team works using AI, built approaches others can follow, and you carefully verify what the tools give you

· Experience with treasury management systems such as Kyriba or equivalent

· Open banking exposure in an AP or AR context

· Multi-entity, multi-currency ERP configuration experience

· Background in e-invoicing or ERP compliance and regulatory delivery

· Consulting background, ideally with a move into in-house product or delivery

This role requires a strategic builder who can operate without a pre-existing playbook. You will make consequential prioritization decisions, turn ambiguous opportunities into a coherent roadmap, and lead across Product, Design, Engineering, Data, Product Marketing, Search Engine Optimization, Brand, and Growth. Your success will be measured by the outcomes the web experience creates, not by the volume of pages launched or requests completed.

· Set the web product vision and roadmap. Define the long-term strategy for postman.com and related web properties. Establish how our web surfaces work together as a portfolio, which audiences and jobs they serve, and where we should invest to create the greatest customer and business value.

· Expand product discovery and top-of-funnel reach. Create new ways for people to discover Postman's full product suite, capabilities, use cases, and solutions. Identify underserved audiences and high-potential entry points, then turn them into intuitive, scalable web experiences.

· Own the most important web journeys. Map and improve the end-to-end paths from first visit through evaluation and entry into the product. Reduce friction, clarify value, and ensure the handoff between the public web experience and the authenticated product feels coherent.

· Build a trusted analytics and attribution foundation. Partner with Data and Engineering to define instrumentation, event taxonomy, source and campaign attribution, identity stitching, funnel reporting, and decision-quality dashboards. Ensure we can understand what is working, for whom, and why.

· Lead privacy-aware measurement. Have a strong point of view on first-party and third-party cookies, consent management, browser restrictions, data retention, and regional privacy requirements. Balance measurement quality, user trust, and compliance when making product decisions.

· Make technical search optimization a product capability. Own the product strategy for technical search (agent) engine optimization, including site architecture, crawlability, indexation, rendering, structured data, internal linking, redirects, canonicalization, and large-scale content or domain migrations.

· Raise the bar for web performance and quality. Set clear standards for page speed, Core Web Vitals, accessibility, reliability, responsiveness, and cross-browser behavior. Work with Design and Engineering to make craft and performance reinforcing rather than competing priorities.

· Lead through influence. Bring together senior partners across Product, Marketing, Design, Engineering, Data Science, Analytics, and Search Engine Optimization. Communicate strategy, decisions, results, and learning to executive audiences with clarity and conviction.

· Build for a global audience. Develop a thoughtful approach to internationalization and localization so that Postman's web experiences can perform across markets, languages, and regional customer needs.

Your foundation is product management. You bring enough fluency across growth, marketing, design, analytics, privacy, and web engineering to lead effectively at the seams, but you have built your career by owning products and outcomes.

Nebius is leading a new era in cloud infrastructure for the global AI economy. We are building a full-stack AI cloud platform that supports developers and enterprises from data and model training through to production deployment, without the cost and complexity of building large in-house AI/ML infrastructure.
Built by engineers, for engineers. From large-scale GPU orchestration to inference optimization, we own the hard problems across compute, storage, networking and applied AI.
Listed on Nasdaq (NBIS) and headquartered in Amsterdam, we have a global footprint with R&D hubs across Europe, the UK, North America and Israel. Our team of 1,500+ includes hundreds of engineers with deep expertise across hardware, software and AI R&D.

Our customers build the frontier of AI on top of Nebius — training state-of-the-art models, running production inference at scale, shipping the research and products that define where the field is going next.
We are building the AI cloud that the people building the frontier of AI choose deliberately — not on price, not on raw capacity, but on how it works to use it day to day. To do that, we are growing the AI Compute Platform product team and hiring multiple Technical Product Managers across the full surface of the platform.
Your scope will be defined by what you bring. We will match your technical strengths, customer experience, and product instincts to the area of the platform where you can have the most impact. The platform is broad — and at our scale, every slice is mission-critical.
If you want to help build the best AI cloud in the world — and you have the technical depth to engage engineering leaders as a peer (not as a translator) and the comfort to talk to customers directly — this team is for you.

Hardware platforms & launch — bringing new GPU and CPU platforms (GB300, Vera Rubin, ARM/Grace, future generations) to production with full launch readiness across the stack.
Cluster lifecycle & fleet operations — new region launches, 100,000+ GPU cluster bring-up, platform sharding and allocation architecture, release engineering, host-lifecycle automation, operational efficiency.
Reliability & Mission Control — autohealing, health checks, SLA, fault-tolerant training, MTTR reduction, customer trust at scale, observability as a product.
Customer experience & developer surface — Compute APIs, console, CLI, IMDS and in-VM signals, self-service workflows, notifications, customer-facing observability, unified UX across the product line.
GPU & InfiniBand foundational services — drivers, firmware, NCCL, IB/RoCE, NVLink topology, the foundational layer everything else builds on.
Managed runtime platforms — Soperator (Slurm-on-Kubernetes) and MK8S (Managed Kubernetes for AI workloads), powering training and inference for frontier labs.
Platform integrations & emerging workloads — Token Factory integration, RL and agentic workload infrastructure, capacity sharing, new business surfaces as they emerge.
Cross-platform program & delivery — NVIDIA partnership programs, major-maintenance orchestration, cross-stream releases.
You will own one of the slices of this platform end-to-end — from strategy and roadmap through delivery, adoption, and measurable outcomes.
Your responsibilities will include (regardless of which slice you own):
Own end-to-end product responsibility for your area — strategy, roadmap, discovery, delivery, adoption, measurable customer and platform outcomes.
Design and own the platform contracts customers depend on — APIs, semantics, system events, customer-facing surfaces, operational behavior — at hyperscaler quality.
Drive cross-team execution across platform engineering, networking, storage, Soperator/MK8S, observability, IAM, billing, capacity planning, support, and product design.
Turn customer pain into product commitments through structured discovery — interviews, usage analytics, support patterns, incident postmortems. Close the loop so the same class of failure or friction does not recur.
Engage engineering as a technical peer — debate API design, reason about system trade-offs, judge the quality of platform internals, and push back when the design is wrong.
Define and own success metrics — what you ship is measured by what changed for the customer or the platform, not by the size of the spec.
Be the product voice that customer-facing teams (Support, CX, TAMs) escalate to when a system behavior, API contract, or operational pattern needs a product decision, not a workaround.

6+ years in Product Management, Platform PM, Infrastructure PM, or SRE / Engineering Lead with strong product instincts.
Strong technical foundation and cloud-infrastructure depth — comfort reasoning about API semantics, control-plane vs data-plane behavior, system events and lifecycle, multi-tenant operational realities. You can engage engineering leaders as a peer, not as a translator.
Experience with cloud, GPU, or HPC infrastructure — either building one or operating one at meaningful scale (thousands of nodes, multi-region, multi-tenant).
Track record of shipping technically complex platform products with measurable customer or platform impact — quantitative results, not aspirational bullets.
Strong analytical skills: comfort defining and instrumenting product metrics, working with telemetry, building data-informed roadmaps.
Experience leading discovery-heavy work — structured customer interviews, usage analytics, support-ticket analysis — and turning insights into shipped product.
Strong communication and ability to align engineering, SRE, customer-facing teams, and exec stakeholders.
High ownership, bias to ship, comfort with messy operational reality, and the instinct to push back on engineering when the customer experience or platform quality would suffer.
It will be an added bonus if you have (these are not all required — different strengths fit different slices of the platform):

Direct PM experience with frontier AI customers — ML platform teams, MLOps engineers, training and inference at scale.
Familiarity with Kubernetes, Slurm, or HPC environments from the user side, and ML training workflows.
Hands-on experience with ML training and inference workflows — especially distributed training at scale (multi-node, multi-GPU; comfort with checkpointing, NCCL, fault-tolerant training, debugging large training jobs).
Experience as a customer of AI cloud infrastructure at large scale — especially as part of an internal ML platform team that built and operated infrastructure for ML engineers inside your own company. If you have lived through what frustrates customers about clouds, you will know exactly what we are trying to fix.

Direct experience with NVIDIA reference architectures (NVL72, SuperPOD, MGX, DGX) and the NVIDIA stack (drivers, CUDA, NCCL, DCGM).
Familiarity with InfiniBand / RoCE fabrics, firmware lifecycle, topology-aware scheduling.
Hands-on with GPU clusters or HPC fabrics at thousands-of-nodes scale.
Background in Kubernetes lifecycle (CAPI, cluster upgrades, node-pool management) or Slurm at scale.

Human Interest is on a mission to ensure that people in all lines of work have access to retirement benefits. More than half of all working Americans are not saving enough for their future. Too often, it’s because they are employed by a company that doesn’t offer a retirement plan.

Human Interest is changing that by making it affordable and accessible for small and medium-sized businesses to offer employees a path to financial independence through retirement savings. We’re a high-growth fintech company changing the retirement industry. We are backed by a number of investors.

This includes funding from Marshall Wace and Baillie Gifford, as well as top investors such as BlackRock , TPG (The Rise Fund) , SoftBank, Glynn Capital , NewView Capital, USVP, Wing, Uncork, and more. About the role Product management is changing.

The best product managers no longer just write requirements and wait for engineering; they prototype their own ideas, pressure-test them with data, and use AI to move from problem to validated solution in days rather than quarters.

We are looking for senior product managers who have internalized that shift and who want to apply it to one of the biggest unsolved problems in America: helping working people save for retirement.

You will own the product strategy for a meaningful surface area, lead a roadmap for a dedicated engineering team, and partner across Engineering, Design, Operations, Revenue, Customer Success, and Compliance to deliver accurate, timely, and transparent outcomes at scale.

You will do this as an AI-augmented builder: using modern AI tooling both to sharpen how you work and to shape products that increasingly work on our customers’ behalf. What you get to do every day Own the vision and strategy for your product area end to end.

Set a clear, opinionated direction, define the outcomes that matter, and rally your team and stakeholders behind a roadmap that delivers a great customer experience while achieving business goals and satisfying regulatory requirements.

Define and own the goals that measure success, quantify the business impact of what you ship, and rigorously track and report progress on a weekly and monthly basis. Produce artifacts that unblock engineering teams to deliver high-quality work on time.

Partner with other product teams so your solutions deliver a great end-to-end platform experience, not just a strong local one. Dig into the data from first principles, form a point of view, and use it to validate assumptions and drive decisions.

Navigate tradeoffs and negotiate timelines with internal and external stakeholders, communicating with precision in both writing and conversation. How you work with AI We expect our senior product managers to use AI to work smarter and solve problems faster, and to bring good judgment about where AI belongs in the product itself. Prototype rapidly.

Use tools such as Figma Make, Claude Code, Codex, or similar to explore, validate, and demonstrate new ideas yourself, so you can align a team on direction with a working artifact rather than a document. Compress the busywork .

Apply AI to speed up research synthesis, requirements drafting, data exploration, and analysis so you spend your time on judgment, strategy, and customer understanding. Build AI into the product.

Identify where copilots, agents, and intelligent automation genuinely improve the customer experience, and partner with engineering on what to build and how it should behave across success, failure, and edge cases.

What you bring to the role Experience: 5+ years of product management experience, including owning a roadmap for a dedicated engineering team in a technical product area. Experience with financial or other regulated products is a strong plus.

AI fluency: Demonstrated, hands-on use of AI tools to build and transform how you work, not just as a chatbot. You are comfortable vibe-coding front-end and UX changes yourself, and you can point to prototypes or interfaces where AI meaningfully changed the outcome or the pace. Builder mindset: High agency and high urgency.

You own problems end to end, turn zero-to-one ideas into real products, and do whatever it takes to execute complex projects. Technical partnership: You have partnered closely with engineers on complex systems at scale, can self-sufficiently root-cause issues, and can propose credible fixes.

Analytical rigor: You are data-driven and think from first principles, and you are equally excited about 100 percent accuracy and 99 percent timeliness. Business acumen: You enjoy digging into how a business works, identifying how to make it better, and building product and technical solutions to do so.

Communication: Crisp, high-attention-to-detail written and verbal communication, with the ability to make complex technical concepts clear to any audience. Education: Degree in Computer Science, Business, or a related field.

Our PRM (Partner Relationship Management) platform is the operating system for MongoDB's entire partner ecosystem — the system partners and internal teams rely on for onboarding, deal registration, enablement content, incentives, and reporting.

We're looking for a Director, Business Product Manager to own the business vision and requirements for this platform: the strategic counterpart to the engineering/IT team that builds it.

This is a business-side role — you won't be writing code — but you need to understand PRM deeply enough to translate partner and internal stakeholder needs into a clear product vision, a prioritized roadmap, and requirements engineering can build against.

You'll report to the VP of Partner Strategic Operations and work as the connective tissue between the partner organization (Sales Plays & Offerings, Programs, Enablement, Digital Process & AI Operations) and the engineering/IT teams who build and maintain the platform.

We are looking to speak to candidates who are based anywhere in the US for our hybrid working model.

Own the vision and strategy

· Define and own the long-term business vision and strategy for the PRM platform, anchored in the needs of partners and internal partner-organization stakeholders.

· Build and maintain a prioritized product roadmap that balances competing demands from Sales Plays & Offerings, Programs, Enablement, Digital Process & AI Operations, and field/partner-facing teams.

· Stay current on PRM market direction (Salesforce PRM, Impartner, Workspan, Zift, Crossbeam, and emerging AI-native entrants) to inform build-vs-buy and platform evolution decisions.

· Run structured discovery with stakeholders across the partner organization to surface needs, pain points, and opportunities, and translate them into clear, prioritized requirements.

· Author business requirements documents (BRDs), user stories, and acceptance criteria that engineering and IT can build against without ambiguity.

· Maintain and groom the product backlog, balancing new capability requests against platform stability, data quality, and technical debt considerations raised by engineering.

Work cross-functionally to deliver

· Act as the primary business-side liaison to Engineering/IT and any implementation partners or vendors, ensuring business intent survives translation into technical delivery.

· Partner closely with the Digital Process & AI Operations lead to align on which PRM capabilities should be built as native platform features versus automations layered on top.

· Lead or participate in UAT (user acceptance testing) cycles to confirm delivered functionality meets business requirements before release.

· Drive change management and adoption for new PRM capabilities — communication, training materials, and enablement content in partnership with the Enablement team.

Measure and iterate

· Define and track adoption and health metrics for the PRM platform (partner activation, feature adoption, ticket/escalation volume, NPS or satisfaction where available).

· Report platform performance and roadmap progress to the VP of Partner Strategic Operations and other partner-organization stakeholders on a regular cadence.

· Continuously reprioritize the roadmap based on usage data, stakeholder feedback, and evolving partner-ecosystem strategy.

· 8+ years of experience in product management, business systems, or business analysis roles, ideally with direct exposure to PRM, CRM, or other partner/channel technology platforms at a B2B SaaS or infrastructure/data company.

· Deep working knowledge of how a PRM platform functions — partner onboarding, deal registration, MDF/incentive tracking, tiering, co-sell workflows — even without hands-on engineering or configuration experience.

· A track record of authoring clear BRDs, user stories, and acceptance criteria, and successfully partnering with engineering/IT teams to deliver against them.

· Strong cross-functional stakeholder management — comfortable gathering and reconciling competing requirements from multiple partner-organization teams and prioritizing transparently.

· Executive presence and communication skills; able to represent the business vision to senior leadership and translate technical constraints back to business stakeholders in plain language.

· Experience running or participating in UAT, change management, and adoption efforts for enterprise platform rollouts.

· Comfortable operating as a strategic business owner rather than a technical builder — this role does not require coding, scripting, or platform administration skills, but does require enough technical fluency to have credible, detailed conversations with engineering.

Job Description
At Docplanner, we run the #1 patient–doctor marketplace in most of the markets where we operate, connecting over 100 million patients every month with the doctors and clinics who care for them. Our mission is simple: to help people live longer, healthier lives.
Doctors and clinics pay to be on our marketplace because it delivers something they can measure – patients, bookings, and real return on their investment. The Visibility team exists to guarantee that outcome. When a doctor or clinic buys our Marketplace product, this team makes sure they are set up well, get found by the right patients, fill their calendars, and clearly see the ROI that keeps them with us for years.
As Senior Product Manager for Visibility, you will own the product and business logic that decides how doctors are ranked and surfaced across the marketplace, together with the paid visibility products (First Class, Media360) that let them grow further.

You will work hand in hand with Customer Success and Patient Marketing to turn a new customer into a thriving, retained one – distributing patient demand intelligently, reducing “zero-booking” doctors, and lifting retention and lifetime value across the base.
This is a highly commercial, deeply analytical product role at the core of how our marketplace creates value for both patients and the professionals who serve them.

Owning Doctor Success strategy and outcomes
Co-own the core success and health metrics for the marketplace customer base: retention, churn and the reduction of zero-booking (“zero-UB”) doctors.
Partner with Customer Success and Patient Marketing to set doctors up for success from onboarding through renewal, closing the loop between how a profile is configured and the bookings it generates.
Design differentiated success journeys for different customer segments, specialties, and maturity levels.
Owning ranking, relevance, and visibility logic
Own the business logic that governs how doctors and clinics are ranked, matched, and surfaced across marketplace search and listings.
Balance patient experience and relevance against doctor outcomes and commercial objectives, and define the guardrails that keep that balance healthy.
Define evaluation frameworks, success metrics, and experiments to measure and continuously improve ranking quality.
Owning paid visibility and growth products
Own the roadmap and business logic for our paid visibility products, including First Class (premium placement) and Media360 (managed patient-acquisition media).
Make the value of these products transparent to customers, so the ROI is obvious and repeatable.
Working data-first
Use SQL and analytics tools daily to answer your own questions, size opportunities, and validate decisions – without waiting on someone else to pull the numbers.
Instrument products well, define the metrics that matter, and build the dashboards and experiments the team runs on.
Drive an experimentation culture: form hypotheses, run A/B tests, read the results honestly, and iterate.
Operating as an AI-native Product Manager
Use AI tools such as Claude, Claude Code, Cursor, and AI prototyping tools daily to accelerate discovery, prototyping, PRD creation, and execution.
Move quickly from research and discovery to validation, launch, and iteration using AI-assisted workflows.
Collaborating across teams
Work closely with Customer Success, Patient Marketing, Engineering, Data, Design, and country teams to deliver impact across markets.
Use qualitative and quantitative research to inform decisions and optimise customer outcomes.
Help evolve our marketplace and AI-native product practices and level up the wider product organisation.
What will set you up for success in this role?
Core Product Management experience
5+ years of Product Managemen t experience building digital consumer or marketplace products .
Strong product thinking and a user-centric mindset, paired with the commercial instinct to connect product decisions to business outcomes.
Excellent communication and stakeholder-management skills across both commercial and technical audiences.
Experience working cross-functionally with Engineering, Design, and Data teams.
Extreme ownership, comfortable operating in ambiguity and shaping products in emerging spaces.
Exceptionally data-driven
Fluent with SQL and comfortable querying large datasets to explore, size, and validate opportunities independently.
Proven ability to translate business logic into ranking, scoring, or matching logic – and to reason clearly about the trade-offs.
Strong analytical and experimentation skills; you make decisions from data and can defend them.
Deep understanding of customer economics
Strong grasp of the metrics that drive a subscription marketplace: churn, retention, engagement, activation, ARPU, and lifetime value.
Experience owning or moving retention and engagement metrics for a customer base, not just shipping features.

Supabase is the open-source Postgres development platform that 7M+ developers and thousands of enterprises depend on every day. We provide a complete backend solution including Database, Auth, Storage, Edge Functions, Realtime, and Vector Search. All services are deeply integrated and designed for growth.

We’re looking for a Product Manager, Marketplace to join our Product Team to lead our marketplace and integration surfaces.
The marketplace is the two-sided surface of the Supabase ecosystem. On one side, Partners and developers build integrations on top of Supabase primitives like Auth, Storage, and Edge Functions, then publish them for the world to use. On the other, our developers come to discover new capabilities and wire them into their projects without leaving their workflow. Done well, it is the shortest path between a developer with a problem and the exact capability that solves it.
That surface is about to matter more than ever. As the number of capabilities explodes, and as agents begin to assemble software on a developer's behalf, the marketplace becomes the distribution and discovery layer for the whole ecosystem: how both developers and, increasingly, their agents find, trust, and compose what they need. This role owns it.

Own the product strategy and roadmap for the marketplace, the two-sided surface where Partners and developers publish integrations and where Supabase's developer customers discover and install them.
Make it effortless for a developer to find the right capability and integrate it. Own discovery, search, listings, and the whole path from install to working integration, so a new capability connects to Supabase primitives and runs inside a developer's project with minimal glue code.
Make publishing an integration fast and rewarding, so Partners and developers bring their best work to the marketplace and keep it current, and so the catalog stays deep where developers need it.
Set the quality bar and the listing standards, and build the review, guardrail, and versioning mechanisms, with Engineering and our Partnerships team, that keep the catalog trustworthy as it scales.
Own what a healthy marketplace looks like: define the metrics across both supply and demand, instrument the surface end to end, and let the signal rather than opinion drive what gets built next.
Position the marketplace as the distribution layer for agent-driven development, where capabilities get discovered and composed on a builder's behalf rather than browsed and installed by hand.

s.h: You might be a good fit if you
s.t:
Have 7+ years of product management on developer tools or marketplaces , or are an ex-founder with strong product instincts, and can identify which partners and integrations will matter most, with particular instinct for the agentic and code-first integrations now defining how developers build.
Have built and grown a two-sided surface: an app store, a plugin or integration ecosystem, a developer platform, or a marketplace, and understand the chicken-and-egg of balancing supply and demand, recruiting developers, driving listing quality, and making discovery and install effortless for the consuming side. Experience with app stores or developer-platform distribution is a strong plus.
Are biased toward speed , and would rather ship something imperfect and learn than spend another sprint polishing a spec.
Build with what you own, using the marketplace from both sides: publishing a test integration the way a Partner would, and sourcing and wiring one into a project the way a developer would. You form opinions through first-hand use.
Use AI tools to compress the slow parts of the job, like research, drafting, and synthesising feedback, so you spend more time on judgment calls.
Work async by default. Supabase is fully remote, so you make decisions in writing and move work forward without meetings.

Fully Remote
We hire globally. We believe you can do your best work from anywhere. There are no Supabase offices, but we provide a WeWork membership or co-working allowance you can use anywhere in the world.

Every team member receives ESOP (equity ownership) in the company. We want everyone to share in the upside of what we’re building together.
Tech Allowance
Use this budget to set up your ideal work environment—laptop, monitor, headphones, or whatever helps you do your best work.

Supabase covers 100% of health insurance for employees and 80% for dependents, wherever you are. Your wellbeing and your family’s health are important to us.
Annual Off-Sites
Once a year, the entire company gathers in a new city for a week of connection, collaboration, and fun. It’s a highlight of our year.
Flexible Work
We operate asynchronously and trust you to manage your own time. You know what needs to be done and when.
Professional Development
Every team member receives an annual education allowance to spend on learning—courses, books, conferences, or anything that supports your growth.

The Ads Marketplace team is a strategic growth engine for Reddit Ads. Our mission is to democratize high-performance advertising by enabling brands to achieve world-class results with minimal friction. To achieve this, we need an incredibly robust, scalable, and state-of-the-art Machine Learning infrastructure.

Partner with our Velo team to bring our AI business guide to the center of our logged in experience, leveraging the unique capabilities of our agentic platform to do more for our business owners.

Collaborate closely with the product managers who own our individual products — formations, compliance, marketing, and fintech — to bring the best of each into a single, coherent customer experience. Identify and run experiments to lift core engagement, retention, and product-attachment metrics.

Work cross-functionally with design, engineering, and marketing to execute against that vision. Drive usage and attachment of our highest-value products Drive activation across our product suite by directly leading activation initiatives and equipping other PMs with the tools to drive activation themselves.

If a customer paid for it, your job is to get them to use it. Drive higher activation and usage of our key formations, compliance, marketing, and fintech products by surfacing the right capability at the right moment.

Increase awareness and attachment of our highest-value products through thoughtful CTAs, cross-sell sequencing, and upsell entry points — without compromising the customer experience. Use experimentation and customer data to find friction in the purchase funnel and optimize conversion at every step.

Act as the primary Product point of contact across product marketing, customer success, finance, and other teams that contribute to increasing customer attach rate and retention.

Operate as a builder Use AI across the product lifecycle — research, ideation, prototyping, experiment design — with tools like Claude, Lovable, v0, and Replit as your default mode of working, not a one-off. Prototype your high-potential ideas and put them in front of real customers or internal users for rapid feedback and iteration.

Contribute to our product features that create real customer value — with the judgment to know where AI deepens the experience vs. where it's a distraction. What We're Looking For 6+ years of product management experience, with at least 2 years at a Staff or senior PM level.

Proven track record owning mobile app products (iOS and/or Android) — you understand the platform, the patterns, and how to drive engagement on native surfaces. Demonstrated ability to design unified experiences across multiple products and partner closely with other PMs to make the whole greater than the sum of its parts.

Experience designing self-serve customer experiences with thoughtful escalation paths to human support. Strong instincts around monetization — you know how to position products, write CTAs, structure purchase flows, and find the friction that kills conversion.

Experience working across web and native apps simultaneously; you think in customer journeys, not platforms. Strong collaborator with design and engineering; you can drive decisions without authority. Comfortable in ambiguity — this role requires you to set direction, not execute someone else's roadmap.

About the role Automated video editing is an emerging category, and we're positioned to define it. Media companies want to turn thousands of podcast episodes into social clips. Marketing teams want to automatically create product demos for every release. Agencies want to process client content in bulk with consistent branding.

And they want to do all of that at scale. As the Product Manager for this 0 to 1 area, you'll build and own the platform that makes this all possible. You'll create APIs that let developers programmatically import media, run AI-powered edits, and export content.

As a Product Manager in PPRO’s Local Payments Domain, you will play a pivotal role in shaping the payment experiences for our customers and partners, ensuring seamless, compliant, and efficient access to local payment methods. Product Managers at PPRO have the passion and abilities for ensuring that we focus our time and energy on building the right things for our customers. You will inform the strategy, communicate with all relevant stakeholders and lead effective product discoveries with your team.

Our mission is to make local payment methods as ubiquitous and accessible as credit cards. You will own and develop a portfolio of Local Payments integrations, engaging with schemes, defining a strong value proposition, and validating and setting success metrics.

Execute and inform our product strategy for our local payments portfolio from scheme engagement to product feature development and market launch.
Drive product discovery and delivery - collaborate with engineers and stakeholders to develop innovative, "Better-than-direct" payment experiences that drive value for our business and customers.
Develop and optimise the payments product portfolio that balances scheme requirements, financial efficiency, and high success rates for consumers and merchants.
Work hands-on with data - analyze key business opportunities and success metrics related to payment acceptance rates, scheme performance, and financial flow efficiency to drive meaningful outcomes.
Define clear success metrics and KPIs to measure payment method efficiency, automate reporting, and enable data-driven decision-making.
Collaborate cross-functionally – work closely with Compliance, Risk, Sales, and Customer Success teams to refine payment requirements, implement new features, and understand business needs.
Inform the roadmap planning and lead the execution for key initiatives, such as the strategic integration of new local payment methods, optimization of existing flows, and co-creation of new products with schemes.
Be a thought leader in local payments – stay ahead of regulatory changes, market trends, and best practices to keep PPRO at the forefront of effective, efficient, and accessible payments across the world.
What Success Looks Like
Improved adoption and financial performance of the local payments portfolio through optimization and strategic feature releases.
Higher payment success rates and fewer manual interventions for payment flows.
Seamless integration and expansion of new local payment methods and features into the core PPRO platform, replacing legacy integration methods.
Clear, data-driven insights into payment performance (acceptance rates, authorization rates, scheme metrics), with real-time visibility for internal stakeholders.
Positive feedback from customers and partners on the functionality, reliability, and value derived from the local payment methods.
